goal: Inspect this ceramic tile for defects. Single static image from a fixed camera: no other viewpoints or lighting exist.

findings.description: Upper-right corner has a region with a rough, grainy, bright-speckled texture and a hazy look. It differs from the smooth glossy glaze with dark speckles seen over the rest of the surface. The boundary with the normal area is gradual and diffuse.
hypotheses: Glaze texture variation or thin glaze
Specular glare or reflection on a locally uneven surface
Edge of the tile or a different surface region at the image corner

findings.description: In the top-right corner of the second image there is a localized region with a rough, grainy, bright-speckled texture. It looks different from the smooth glazed surface with dark mottling seen elsewhere and in the reference. The reference has no such patch.
hypotheses: glaze defect such as pitting or abrasion
specular glare or reflection on the glaze

proposed=insufficient_evidence, sufficient=False. PROC-CT-004 is the static single-view procedure for ceramic tile and replaces the multi-view criteria of PROC-CT-001, so those cannot be checked here. PROC-CT-002 covers crazing versus cracks; obs_01 shows no hairline network or dominant line, so it does not apply. The upper-right corner of obs_01 is a rough, grainy region with a hazy look, which could be a 'Rough' defect under CT-4. However, CT-4 requires a comparison with the approved reference, and the reference has not been fetched (matches_reference=None, 'no earlier observation to compare against'). The finding's uncertainty is high, and hypotheses include glare and a corner or edge effect. A defect verdict is therefore unsupported, and so is a no-defect verdict. The reference must be fetched and compared first.

get_reference {'category': 'ceramic_tile'}: The only remaining candidate action is get_reference. It is the cheapest test that differs between hypotheses, because PROC-CT-004 requires comparison with the approved reference before any defect call. Lighting or pose changes are not available (no other poses or lights exist), so the reference comparison is the only way to separate a real Rough defect from normal variation, glare, or a corner artifact. | expects: If the upper-right rough/hazy region is a real defect (Rough), the approved reference will show smooth uniform speckle texture at that corner, so the region has no counterpart. If it is normal variation, glare, or a corner/edge artifact, the reference will show a similar grainy or hazy area at the same location, or the corner will be outside the tile face. The tan specks should appear on the reference too if they are normal decoration; if absent from the reference, they are likely debris or inclusions.
